questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. The biggest danger is when cars turn left in front of motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Maintain eye contact with other road users.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to make your motorcycle visible to others. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the oily strip in the center of the lane becomes very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: Who is required to wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle:

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake can prevent you from developing the skill to use the front brake when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material when riding to make yourself more visible. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's potential stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must let other traffic go first.

questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. Stop completely and wait for a green arrow before turning.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Make sure the paint is not peeling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Check your bike before every ride. Test both brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Traffic law signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to look.
Stop at the stop line and go through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then carefully move forward and stop again just before the crossing lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the cross lane while looking.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands. Paint condition is not part of a safety check.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during the day.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any type of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain starts. Ride in tire tracks left by cars for better grip.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your bike.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in emergencies.
Should be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.
